stories.headline: Jayson Tatum insists 'there's no beef' with Jaylen Brown in wake of trade
stories.summary: Jayson Tatum spent most of his postgame news conference Friday night addressing speculation about his relationship with former Celtics teammate Jaylen Brown in the wake of the latter's shocking trade to Philadelphia over the summer.
stories.body:
BOSTON -- There's been rings and failures, innuendos, rumors and internet emojis, and finally, a trade that ended the Jayson Tatum-Jaylen Brown partnership in Boston.

Tatum spent most of his postgame news conference Friday night addressing Brown sending out a "cap" emoji on Instagram in response to Tatum saying in a video on his YouTube channel that he was "just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world" by Brown's trade to the Philadelphia 76ers this summer.

Asked if he had any response to Brown's social media comment, Tatum sighed before expressing his frustrations with the entire situation for several minutes.

"I don't have any animosity or beef or ill will towards him," Tatum said following the Celtics' 107-103 win over the New York Knicks in Boston's home opener. "The frustrating part is since he's not on the Celtics anymore, the narrative or conversations haven't been enough about what we accomplished, all the games we won, winning the championship, how we've grown together, right?"

Brown was drafted in 2016, Tatum a year later. Together, they helped the Celtics to a Finals win over Dallas in 2024, another Finals appearance in 2022 and the Eastern Conference finals in five of eight years.

Whenever the Celtics underachieved in the playoffs, there were rumors about their relationship and speculation over whether the Celtics would trade one over the other. At times, the partnership felt awkward, but Tatum believes so much has been sensationalized.

"This ain't no f---ing Shaq and Kobe," Tatum said, referring to the highly publicized issues Shaquille O'Neal and the late Kobe Bryant had during their eight years together on the Los Angeles Lakers. "There's no beef, it's not about that. It should be more praise. I understand drama gets clicks and views but I'm not really into that. I'm not blaming everybody for how they feel, everybody is entitled to their own feelings and we all go through different things in our lives."

Tatum repeatedly pointed out that he's a father of two, and multiple times cited a breakdown in communication, stating a conversation shouldn't be had over social media.

"I reached out to him the day he was traded. I called, I texted," Tatum said. "I understand people process things differently. At this point in our lives, we're too old to be having our relationship discussed on the internet. If there's a conversation to be had, we can definitely have the conversation.

"I welcome that. I've always wanted the best for him, wished the best for him. I've always publicly said those things."

Much was made of the 76ers-Celtics preseason matchup in Boston in early October, where it appeared the two didn't interact during pregame warmups. The two teams meet for real on Nov. 10 in Philadelphia.

"I've seen all these things about, 'Get your popcorn ready when they play' -- like this ain't no f---ing boxing match, it's basketball," Tatum said. "I hate the conversation, the narrative around it. There's not enough communication and a conversation will solve or put out a lot of fires."

Both players made All-Star teams and had multiple All-NBA selections. Brown was named Finals MVP in 2024 by a 7-4 margin in voting, and Tatum went to the Olympic Games that summer in France while Brown didn't -- albeit, while not playing much.

Tatum's 36 points, nine rebounds and seven assists Friday marked his best game since Game 4 of the Eastern Conference semifinals two years ago against the Knicks, when he scored 42 points before rupturing his Achilles, an injury that forced him to miss most of last season.

Brown helped carry the Celtics to 56 wins and the No. 2 seed in the East. Tatum returned for the final 16 regular-season games and played in six games in Boston's first-round series against Philadelphia, missing Game 7 with left knee stiffness.

Despite the loss, Brown called it the most fun he has had in a season. He was then traded to the 76ers in a July blockbuster that ended his 10-year tenure in Boston and brought Paul George to the Celtics.

It's been one thing after another since, and Tatum hopes direct contact can put an end to the speculation.

"Just a conversation. Not a bad one or anything like that," Tatum said. "Right, wrong, you can understand the other side. It's not done enough, especially in our business."

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Brewers withstand Rays' comeback attempt to win 3-2 in Game 1 of World Series
stories.summary: — Trevor Megill was shouting in celebration and the Milwaukee Brewers were bolting out of the dugout to congratulate one another, believing they had just escaped a ninth-inning jam to win Game 1 of the World Series.
stories.body:
MILWAUKEE -- — Trevor Megill was shouting in celebration and the Milwaukee Brewers were bolting out of the dugout to congratulate one another, believing they had just escaped a ninth-inning jam to win Game 1 of the World Series.


Not quite yet.


What initially was ruled a game-ending double play got overturned after a video review showed Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt’s right foot was slightly off the bag when he reached to catch a high throw from second baseman Brice Turang.


No problem.


Megill regrouped and struck out Jonny DeLuca with two runners in scoring position as Milwaukee edged the Tampa Bay Rays 3-2 on Friday night.


“It's good to get the first win out of the way,” Megill said. “That's where all the nerves are at. First game, a lot of anticipation and build-up to where we are right now."


The ninth inning was particularly nerve-racking for the Brewers and the sellout crowd attending Milwaukee’s first World Series game since 1982.


“You have a big range of emotions,” said team captain Christian Yelich, whose RBI triple in the first put the Brewers ahead for good. “It’s a big credit to Trev for locking back in right there and making some huge pitches after you have that emotional dump and then have to get back on it.”


Tampa Bay trailed 3-1 and hadn’t put a runner on since the sixth until it mounted its comeback attempt against Megill.


Jonathan Aranda, who went 3 for 3 with a walk, and Chandler Simpson hit consecutive one-out singles. A double steal involving pinch-runner Jorge Mateo and Simpson put runners on second and third before Junior Caminero walked on a 3-2 pitch in the dirt to load the bases.


Liam Hicks hit a grounder to the right side, and Turang ranged well to his left to field the ball before throwing to Pratt to start what initially was called a 4-6-3 double play.


Fireworks went off, players poured onto the field and Milwaukee fans roared. But then the crowd hushed as it watched the play again on the videoboard.


“You've got to think worst-case scenario there,” Megill said. “I thought the challenge was at first base, maybe a bobble or something. But it was pretty clear once the replay went up that it was on the play at second base. Zoomed in and it didn't look good. It's all right. We picked up Cooper there. He'll pick us up tomorrow.”


The out call at second was changed to safe by umpire Alfonso Márquez at the MLB Replay Center, which caught Pratt by surprise.


“Obviously, it was close,” the 22-year-old rookie said. “I just didn't think it was enough to overturn, so I wasn't thinking anything of it. The video I saw, thought my cleat was dragging. ... There must have been some other angles that I haven't seen. It ultimately didn't matter because we won.”


The Brewers won because Megill got DeLuca to swing and miss at a 2-2 pitch, capping a night in which Tampa Bay went 0 for 6 with runners in scoring position.


“This is an extremely confident group,” Rays manager Kevin Cash said. “You know that. We know that. They’re going to be fine. I think the frustration comes from we were one swing of the bat away right at the end of potentially taking the lead.”


The Game 1 winner has gone on to win the World Series 62.8% of the time.


This marks the first World Series featuring two teams seeking their first championship since 1980, when the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Kansas City Royals in six games. The only other major league clubs without a World Series title are the Colorado Rockies, San Diego Padres and Seattle Mariners.


Milwaukee took a 2-0 lead in the first inning against Nick Martinez. NL Cy Young Award favorite Jacob Misiorowski allowed one run and four hits over five innings to help the Brewers stay in front before relievers Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby shut down the Rays through the eighth.


Misiorowski, who had a season-low three strikeouts, opened the game with a 103.5 mph fastball — the fastest pitch ever thrown in a World Series.


“The adrenaline kind of took over, and I tensed up and threw it hard,” said Misiorowski, who earned the win. “Then I settled down, and that was the game plan, to settle in and do me. Don’t try and overdo it.”


Milwaukee's Jackson Chourio and William Contreras each had two hits, including an RBI single. Contreras also threw out two runners trying to steal.


Tampa Bay managed to hang around thanks in part to Martinez, who gave up those two runs in the first but held Milwaukee scoreless through the rest of his five-inning stint. The Brewers added an insurance run in the seventh when Chourio singled home Pratt.


Then came all the action in the ninth, with the Brewers' premature celebration followed by a team-wide sigh of relief as Pratt offered some parting words to Megill.


“I just said, ‘Thank you, man. Thanks for picking me up,’” Pratt said. “That’s what this game is. It's a game of pick-me-up. He picked me up today.”


Up next
Drew Rasmussen (16-5, 2.67 ERA) pitches for Tampa Bay and Logan Henderson (11-3, 2.47) starts for Milwaukee in Game 2 on Saturday night. In this postseason, Rasmussen is 2-0 with a 1.29 ERA and Henderson is 0-0 with a 3.00 ERA.

stories.headline: Nathan MacKinnon has goal and 3 assists in Avalanche's 6-3 win over Lightning
stories.summary: — Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists, Nazem Kadri scored his first goal of the season and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Tampa Bay...
stories.body:
DENVER -- — Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists, Nazem Kadri scored his first goal of the season and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-3 on Friday night.


Devon Toews, Fedor Svechkov, Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Necas also scored as Colorado rebounded from back-to-back road losses. Mackenzie Blackwood made 31 saves.


Jake Guentzel scored twice and Charle-Edouard D’Astous added another for the Lightning, who saw their three-game winning streak halted. Nikita Kucherov was held in check and remains a goal or assist away from becoming the franchise's career points leader. He has 1,137 points and is tied with Steven Stamkos.


Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 18 of 23 shots, including one off the mask on MacKinnon's liner.


Guentzel's goal with 42.7 seconds left in the second period made it 4-2. The Avalanche unsuccessfully challenged the play for a missed stoppage. The Lightning went on the power play but couldn't score. They struggled on the power play all evening.


MacKinnon’s goal with 15:42 remaining gave Colorado a 5-2 cushion. Necas sealed it with a late empty-net tally.


Logan O’Connor returned to the lineup after missing the start of the season with a lower-body injury. He recently lost his father, Myles, a former NHL defenseman, at age 59.


The game featured the league's currently longest-tenured coaches in Jon Cooper and Jared Bednar. Cooper took over the Lightning in March 2013 and has won two Stanley Cups. Bednar was hired by Colorado in August 2016 and captured one Cup — in 2022 over the Lightning.


Wyndham Clark, the 2026 U.S. Open champion, was in attendance and brought his trophy. Clark drank from the cup while receiving an ovation from the crowd.


Up next
Lightning: At Utah on Saturday night.


Avalanche: At Nashville on Sunday night.

stories.headline: Fever fire GM, president steps down: What's next for Clark and Indiana?
stories.summary: Indiana's president stepped down and the Fever GM was fired Friday. What's next for a team with title aspirations?
stories.byline: Kareem Copeland and Michael Voepel and Alexa Philippou
stories.body:
The Indiana Fever haven't played basketball in more than three weeks, but they still made shockwaves during the WNBA Finals.

News dropped Friday morning that team president Kelly Krauskopf is stepping down after nearly three decades at Pacers Sports & Entertainment. Hours later, the organization announced the firing general manager and chief operating officer Amber Cox.

The expectation is that Stephanie White will remain head coach of the Fever, sources told ESPN.

Although the front office will look much different for the Fever next season, the pressure will remain on star Caitlin Clark and the rest of the team to compete for championships. Following last year's miraculous run in which they were five minutes away from advancing to the Finals, the Fever did not make it out of the first round this season, falling to the three-time champion Las Vegas Aces.

Indiana has also been enveloped in a variety of off-court controversies over the past few years as the Fever navigate the intense spotlight that comes with having Clark on the team. At the end of the season, star guard Kelsey Mitchell acknowledged the challenges of playing for the Fever and with Clark due to the extra attention, some negative, that she receives. During those same media exit interviews, Cox said the negative portrayals of Fever fans "have no basis in reality," which former Fever player Brianna Turner disputed on social media.

ESPN reporters Kareem Copeland, Alexa Philippou and Michael Voepel look at what Krauskopf's and Cox's departures mean for the Fever franchise.

Why are the Fever making this move now?

Copeland: Time is of the essence for the Fever. Clark is still on her rookie deal, though eligible for the "EPIC" extension -- a provision included in the latest collective bargaining agreement that allows players to renegotiate the fourth year of their rookie deals and sign three-year extensions. Fair or not, every season she's on the roster will carry championship expectations. Mitchell, who set the WNBA single-season scoring record in 2026, is an unrestricted free agent who made it clear she will explore her options after playing her entire career in Indianapolis. A first-round exit in 2026 fell well short of expectations. Ownership seems unwilling to risk another season of falling short of the ultimate goal with a roster construction that had some holes.

Philippou: Some speculated whether this means Indiana is cleaning house, but it's not that straightforward. It appears that White will remain in her role. And sources told ESPN that when Krauskopf returned to the Fever in the fall of 2024 (after serving as the Indiana Pacers' assistant GM), she never intended to stay in the role long term and only anticipated staying on for two or three years. She also told team leadership before the end of the regular season that she would be leaving, so it's not clear what the relationship, if any, was between her decision and ownership's choice to move on from Cox when they did.

Indiana is in win-now mode. What other pressures or obstacles internally and externally will new front office hires have to manage?

Copeland: Clark admitted that the microscope she's under often envelops those around her. So, all eyes will be on the new hires and every move closely dissected. There has to be a balance of keeping Clark happy personally and professionally with a competitive roster. If Clark doesn't sign the EPIC extension, she will be a restricted free agent in 2028. Keeping her in Indianapolis is an absolute priority. Additionally, the new GM must manage the off-the-court spotlight that includes negative fan behavior online and in person and the reputation that the fanbase has gotten among players on the team and around the league.

Voepel: The Fever have at the very least a perception problem about their fan base. After Cox's comments at media day, the response was swift. "Players inside and outside the organization have repeatedly issued complaints with the Fever fanbase," Turner said on X. "While it's not all Indy fans, it's certainly a trend. To say the attacks have 'no basis in reality' is disingenuous."

Two years ago, then-Connecticut Sun forward Alyssa Thomas specifically pointed to an element of racism in the responses. "In my 11-year career, I've never experienced the racial comments from the Indiana Fever fanbase. It's unacceptable, honestly," Thomas said. "There's no place for it. We've been professional throughout the whole entire thing, but I've never been called the things that I've been called on social media."

The next team president and general manager must address that more effectively. And it has to start right away with the best crisis management advice available.

In her comments, Cox seemed intent on defending a fanbase that has been part of the WNBA for 26 years while also pointing out that negative fan behavior online isn't the same as in an arena. But she came off as dismissive.

Is it fair or accurate to paint a fanbase based on the dregs of social media? No, but this is the situation the Fever find themselves in, and it could impact player personnel. The Fever have the most marketable player in WNBA history in Clark, who is already on her way to becoming the league's best playmaker. The Fever will soon open a luxurious and spacious practice facility that is near Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Indianapolis is one of the more affordable big cities in the United States to live in. There are many reasons the Fever should be able to attract key free agents. But the organization must deal proactively with negative perceptions, even if they did not cause those perceptions.

In addition to re-signing Mitchell, what are the free agency priorities for the Fever?

Copeland: The two biggest holes in the roster are post help for Aliyah Boston, perimeter shooting and a defensive wing. Cox brought in Monique Billings to play alongside Boston, but Billings eventually lost the job to Makayla Timpson, who has unique athleticism but is limited offensively. The Fever were the No. 1 3-point shooting team in the league, but Clark and Mitchell did most of that work. A 3-and-D wing would help spread the floor and take some of the pressure off those two. The defense, especially on the perimeter, was an issue all season, so any new wing must also help in that area.

Who is likely to be considered for the GM role?

Philippou: There isn't a clear successor for Cox (or Krauskopf) in Indiana, and sources around the league are interested to see what direction Pacers Sports & Entertainment president Mel Raines and Fever ownership go. Do they want someone who has GM experience in the WNBA? That hire would be in a similar mold to Cox -- who previously worked for the Sun, Dallas Wings and in the NWSL -- so if they want to try something different, perhaps not. Clare Duwelius -- former Minnesota Lynx GM and current executive vice president/general manager of Unrivaled -- could be worth a call. She is from Iowa and went to Clark's high school but also got to learn the front office ropes from the best of the best in Cheryl Reeve.

What about an up-and-comer? The league has more assistant GMs than ever -- well-respected ones include Brooklyn Cartwright (Atlanta), Jasmine Thomas (Dallas) and Fleur McIntyre (Phoenix) -- given the resources that franchises are now dedicating to building front offices. That said, someone inexperienced might not be desirable given the high stakes and high-pressure nature of the situation.

The Fever also could follow a trend of looking to the NBA for new and perhaps more innovative front office personnel -- the newest WNBA GM, Ariana Andonian of the Los Angeles Sparks, took that path. Whatever route the Fever take, if the goal is for White to remain in Indiana, any new management hires would have to be OK not bringing in their own head coach right away.

Indiana ownership should look to go big -- including with the financial investment for this hire -- because it needs to get this right.

stories.headline: COTA boss addresses driver concerns ahead of United States GP: 'Turn 1 not acceptable in my mind'
stories.summary: Austin's Circuit of the Americas is "in really good shape" everywhere except one spot at Turn 1, according to the venue owner, following a suggestion from Max Verstappen that the circuit's bumpy surface might cause him spine damage.
stories.body:
Austin's Circuit of the Americas is "in really good shape" everywhere except one spot at Turn 1, according to the venue owner, following a suggestion from Max Verstappen that the circuit's bumpy surface might cause him spine damage.

Verstappen said ahead of this weekend's U.S. Grand Prix that COTA's bumpiness has grown "out of control" in recent years, citing a recent World Endurance Championship (WEC) race he watched as well as his own experience from previous seasons.

The Red Bull driver said a check-up of his lower spine showed some damage from the wear and tear of racing.

Reigning world champion Lando Norris backed up Verstappen's concerns, saying he's previously needed headache tablets for the bumpiness he's experienced inside the cockpit at COTA.

Circuit boss Bobby Epstein is confident the situation will not be as extreme as the two drivers predicted, with work done this year to flatten out the tarmac in key areas.

"We don't feel good that there's a bump at the bottom of Turn 1," Epstein told ESPN. "We didn't know about it until this week. We would have fixed it.

"But the other things Max spoke about, all the bumps around the track, we've fixed them. The track is in really good shape.

"I talked to some WEC drivers who said there's no problem. There's one bump at the beginning of [Turn] 1 that is not acceptable in my mind ... It's a dip, not a bump. If it were a bump, we'd sharpen it out, we'd take care of it tomorrow night, or overnight tonight, and that kind of stuff's happened before [at other circuits]. But when it's a dip it's a lot different, there's no easy fix."

- Ferrari's Charles Leclerc sets pace in second practice from Kimi Antonelli at United States Grand Prix

- FIA president hints at long-awaited F1 V8 engine return: 'Watch this space'

- Carlos Sainz on F1 season concluding in Middle East: 'Very difficult to be convinced right now'

Speaking between Friday's two practice sessions, Epstein joked that he had no doubt Verstappen would agree with him after driving on the track.

"Max doesn't say I'm wrong a lot, but he's also right a lot, and he's usually very frank, and I appreciate that about him," Epstein said. "I had no problem with him saying what he said. I think he might be surprised in some areas that bumps he thought were here aren't any more."

Verstappen did not give his opinion after practice -- teams are only required to send one of their two drivers to talk to the media on Fridays, and Isack Hadjar went.

Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas appeared to agree that the circuit has improved from last year.

"They've managed to grind some of the bigger bumps, but it is a fun track," Bottas said, although other drivers suggested the extreme bumpiness has remained.

Alpine's Franco Colapinto was one of them.

"It's a great track to drive at," the Argentine said. "For the drivers to drive F1 around these high-speed corners, it's one of the best tracks in the world. It's a pity that it's so bumpy, because it becomes harsh on the body as well, our backs suffer. It's not the easiest. Hopefully they can improve it for the future."

stories.headline: Fantasy playbook: NFL Week 7 Shadow Reports, lineup locks and projected scores
stories.summary: An all-encompassing look at the matchups to exploit or avoid and lineup locks in fantasy, as well as projected scores for all NFL games.
stories.body:
Welcome to The Playbook for Week 7, which kicked off Thursday night with a game between the Patriots and Bears.

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start advice, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule for the remainder of the season.

All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. "Matchup" is automatically determined using a proprietary metric that factors in raw and volume-adjusted fantasy points allowed to each position by the opposing defense.

DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for games scheduled on days other than Sunday after 1 p.m. ET.

-->

(Editor's note: Projections and rankings will align almost perfectly, but sometimes when a projection is close, a player might be ranked slightly higher or lower because of other factors, including upside or risk. This column is subject to updates during the weekend, although at the very minimum, rankings will be updated on the site and projections will always be updated inside the game leading up to kickoff.)

PIT-NO | SF-ATL | CLE-TEN | IND-MIN | MIA-NYJ | TB-CAR

CIN-BAL | NYG-HOU | DEN-ARI | GB-DET | LAR-LV | KC-SEA | DAL-PHI

New England Patriots @ Chicago Bears
Projected score: Bears 26, Patriots 24

Lineup locks: Drake Maye, D'Andre Swift, A.J. Brown, Luther Burden III

Fantasy Scoop: Welcome back, Colston Loveland! After totaling 24.0 fantasy points during his first five games of the season, Loveland put up 18.5 points on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons. His big game coincided with the triumphant return of Caleb Williams, who completed 30 out of 36 passes in the win. Loveland now leads all tight ends in snaps and is fifth in end zone targets (four), though he's way down in 21st place in receiving yards and has found the end zone just once.

Loveland's strong performance is enough to get him back into the weekly TE1 mix, but we shouldn't get too carried away, as he's hit 12.0 fantasy points only once this season and he had a total of just 3 yards on five targets during Weeks 1-2 (Williams was under center for most of that). Consider Loveland to be a mid-to-back-end TE1 against a Patriots defense that has allowed only one tight end (Brock Bowers) to reach 8.0 fantasy points this season.

Shadow Alert: This is far from a lock, but it's possible Christian Gonzalez shadows Rome Odunze, just like he has done for Garrett Wilson, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and DK Metcalf this season. Odunze aligns on the perimeter 77% of the time, which makes him the most likely candidate to see a lot of Gonzalez, though it's possible New England's top corner aligns at times against Burden (50% perimeter).

Over/under: 49.8 (5th highest)

Win probability: Bears 57% (13th highest)

-->

Pittsburgh Steelers @ New Orleans Saints
Projected score: Steelers 29, Saints 20

Lineup locks: Jaylen Warren, Chris Olave, DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard

Fantasy Scoop: Bernard has graduated to "lineup lock" status following a terrific Week 6 effort in which he caught 11 out of 12 targets for 87 yards and one touchdown. This, after the rookie second-round pick posted a 6-80-0 receiving line on nine targets the week prior. Bernard's production is no fluke, as his route participation (85%) and target share (28%) have been outstanding during the span.

Bernard's short-area role (4.9 aDOT) may limit his explosive plays and scoring upside, but the high volume supplies him with a high floor, especially in PPR formats. It also helps his cause that Pittsburgh is the league's pass-heaviest team near the goal line (their 87% expected pass TD rate and 92% actual pass TD rate are both tops in the NFL). Consider Bernard to be a solid WR3 against a Saints defense that allowed 250 yards to New York Giants wide receivers last week.

Over/under: 49.7 (6th highest)

Win probability: Steelers 81% (3rd highest)

San Francisco 49ers @ Atlanta Falcons
Projected score: 49ers 29, Falcons 22

Lineup locks: Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, Bijan Robinson, Drake London, George Kittle

Fantasy Scoop: Right when it seemed like Kyle Pitts Sr. had fallen off the map (again), the most polarizing tight end in fantasy is back with a vengeance. After opening the 2026 season with a 2-20-0 receiving line on six targets through three games, Pitts improved to 3-47-0 on three targets in Week 4, 5-42-1 on six targets in Week 5 and 5-60-2 on seven targets in Week 6. Although Pitts' route participation has been volatile this season, it has steadied over the past two weeks -- and he also played on a season-high 76% of Atlanta's snaps last Sunday.

Pitts' usage isn't quite as high as it was last season, but as long as his connection with Michael Penix Jr. remains strong, there's enough here to get him back into the weekly TE1 discussion. Of course, we need to downgrade him here in Week 7, as the 49ers have allowed zero touchdowns and the fourth-fewest fantasy points to tight ends this season. Only Trey McBride and Chig Okonkwo have cleared 5.0 points against them.

Over/under: 50.7 (4th highest)

Win probability: 49ers 73% (4th highest)

Cleveland Browns @ Tennessee Titans
Projected score: Browns 17, Titans 16

Lineup locks: Denzel Boston, Carnell Tate

Fantasy Scoop: With Quinshon Judkins sidelined in Week 5, Jaleel McLaughlin led the Cleveland backfield, playing on 37 snaps, carrying the ball nine times for 41 yards and adding 14 yards on four targets. Audric Estime (18 snaps) was also involved and, while he wasn't targeted and was held to 19 yards on nine carries, he did score the team's lone rushing touchdown.

If Judkins returns in Week 7, both McLaughlin and Estime should be on waivers. If Judkins remains out, neither replacement back will be a recommended flex against a solid Titans run defense, though McLaughlin's passing-game work gives him a slight edge if you're in a tough spot. Note that, should Dylan Sampson return from IR and Judkins remain out, it's Sampson who would be the preferred (albeit still uninspiring) flex from this backfield.

Over/under: 32.6 (Lowest)

Win probability: Browns 55% (Lowest)

Indianapolis Colts @ Minnesota Vikings
Projected score: Vikings 26, Colts 16

Lineup locks: Jonathan Taylor, Justin Jefferson

Fantasy Scoop: Keenan Allen set season-high marks in targets (11), receptions (eight) and yardage (82) against the Titans on Sunday. Allen has now handled at least nine targets in all three games since Alec Pierce was placed on IR. The heavy usage has helped him to a respectable 14.7 fantasy points per game, which includes 16-plus points in two of the three outings.

Allen's short-area role (7.9 aDOT) in the Colts' struggling offense will limit his scoring opportunities (one end zone target this season), but the 25% target share he's enjoyed over the last three games is plenty to keep him in the WR3/flex discussion, especially if Tyler Warren remains sidelined.

Of course, we need to downgrade this entire passing game in Week 7 against a Vikings defense that has allowed the third-fewest passing yards and only three passing TDs this season. Minnesota hasn't allowed any wide receivers to clear 12.0 fantasy points in a game since Week 1.

Over/under: 41.9 (12th highest)

Win probability: Vikings 84% (Highest)

Miami Dolphins @ New York Jets
Projected score: Jets 24, Dolphins 14

Lineup locks: Breece Hall, Garrett Wilson

Fantasy Scoop: Omar Cooper Jr. returned from injury on Sunday and made a major impact. The first-round rookie played on 82% of offensive snaps and posted a 6-103-1 receiving line on seven targets. The big game was a surprise after Cooper missed Weeks 2-5 due to a high ankle sprain suffered on the fourth snap of his pro career back in Week 1. It was a positive sign that Cooper immediately leapfrogged Tim Patrick and Isaiah Williams on the depth chart, but it's also notable that Adonai Mitchell was sidelined and Wilson was dealing with shadow coverage from Christian Gonzalez.

Cooper should be on rosters, but he should be considered for a flex spot only if Mitchell remains out this week. Target volume is likely to be at a premium against a struggling Miami team that has faced the fewest WR targets and thus allowed the third-fewest WR fantasy points this season. In five games, only three receivers have reached double-digit fantasy points against Miami -- and none have reached 20.

Over/under: 38.6 (13th highest)

Win probability: Jets 82% (2nd highest)

Tampa Bay Buccaneers @ Carolina Panthers
Projected score: Panthers 24, Buccaneers 21

Lineup locks: Bucky Irving, Chuba Hubbard, Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Emeka Egbuka

Fantasy Scoop: After producing 52 yards and one touchdown on seven touches in Week 5, Egbuka followed that up with 48 yards and one touchdown on seven touches in Week 6. Egbuka's fantasy point totals in the two games (17.2 and 17.8) are a significant step forward after he had failed to reach 12.0 points in any of his prior 12 games.

Egbuka's target volume has been very good -- a 26% share on the season that includes a career-high 16 targets against Pittsburgh on Sunday. Of course, that heavy usage came with Jalon Daniels under center, and Baker Mayfield may return in Week 7. In his three games with Mayfield this season, Egbuka averaged 6.7 targets and 10.9 fantasy PPG.

The Panthers have been solid against receivers this season, though both starting corners remain sidelined and DeVonta Smith just nailed them for 7-75-1 on Sunday. Regardless of which QB is under center, Egbuka has found his way back into the WR2/3 mix.

Over/under: 44.7 (10th highest)

Win probability: Panthers 60% (8th highest)

Cincinnati Bengals @ Baltimore Ravens
Projected score: Bengals 24, Ravens 22

Lineup locks: Joe Burrow, Derrick Henry, Chase Brown, Ja'Marr Chase, Zay Flowers, Tee Higgins

Shadow Report: DJ Turner is a strong bet to shadow Flowers when he aligns on the perimeter, which he has done on 45% of his routes this season. Turner has emerged as one of the league's top shadow corners, having already traveled with Emeka Egbuka (11.3 fantasy points in the game), Xavier Hutchinson (6.7), DK Metcalf (12.1), Parker Washington (2.0) and Chris Bell (2.6) this season.

Turner also shadowed 14 times last season (those receivers averaged 8.8 fantasy PPG), two of which came against Flowers. Flowers was held to a 2-6-0 receiving line on seven targets in the Week 13 matchup, but was better with a 3-68-1 line on five targets in Week 15. Flowers will avoid Turner on roughly half of his routes, but note that the Bengals have allowed a 56% completion rate to receivers (fourth lowest) and none have cleared 15.0 points in a game. Flowers remains a lineup lock, but a down game wouldn't be a shock.

Over/under: 45.9 (9th highest)

Win probability: Bengals 57% (12th highest)

New York Giants @ Houston Texans
Projected score: Texans 30, Giants 24

Lineup locks: C.J. Stroud, Nico Collins, Malik Nabers, Isaiah Likely

Fantasy Scoop: Jaylin Noel caught all four targets for a career-high 107 yards and one touchdown against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 6. Despite the strong game (and despite the fact that he also found the end zone in Week 5), Noel is not yet a viable flex option. The 2025 third-round pick remains a situational player, having yet to eclipse 60% route participation or a 16% target share in any single game of his career.

Noel is trending toward locking down Houston's primary slot receiver job, but that's unlikely to lead to consistent production with so many mouths to feed at wide receiver in that huddle. That list includes Marvin Harrison Jr. (four targets on 11 snaps in his Houston debut), whose role will continue to expand, as well as a now-healthy Tank Dell. At best, Noel is a speculative bench stash, but there's not much upside in the short term.

Over/under: 54.4 (3rd highest)

Win probability: Texans 71% (5th highest)

Denver Broncos @ Arizona Cardinals
Projected score: Broncos 24, Cardinals 21

Lineup locks: Michael Wilson, Trey McBride

Fantasy Scoop: Wilson is a tricky evaluation after a very volatile start to the season. Arizona's top receiver appeared to be primed for a huge season after posting 11-89-1 and 7-95-0 receiving lines on a combined 30 targets during Weeks 3-4. However, he's seen exactly seven targets in his other four games, none of which resulted in more than 10.6 fantasy points. That includes a pair of duds since Harrison's departure, a 4-30-0 showing in an elite matchup against Detroit in Week 5 and a 4-32-0 line against the Trent McDuffie-less Rams last week.

Although the production has been inconsistent, Wilson checks a lot of boxes, including ranking no lower than eighth among receivers in snaps, routes, target share, targets, end zone targets and air yards. As long as that keeps up, he'll find his way to plenty of big games. Wilson is a WR3 against Denver, though you should note that he'll be a candidate for shadow coverage from Pat Surtain II if the standout corner returns from injury.

Over/under: 44.7 (11th highest)

Win probability: Broncos 61% (7th highest)

Green Bay Packers @ Detroit Lions
Projected score: Lions 30, Packers 28

Lineup locks: Jordan Love, Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, Sam LaPorta, Tucker Kraft

Fantasy Scoop: When we last saw the Lions in action (Week 5), Jameson Williams scored his only two touchdowns of the season during a 45-21 win over Arizona. It was Williams' second-consecutive game with 16-plus fantasy points after he fell short of 9.0 points in each of his first three games of the season. The good news is that Williams' playing time has been excellent (89% route participation), but the concern is that his targets have been extremely volatile. He's reached eight targets twice but has seen exactly four targets in the other three games (including the two-TD outing).

Williams' 15.4% target share is his lowest since 2023 and will need to increase in order to allow consistent fantasy production. The speedy receiver should be viewed as a WR3 this week against a Green Bay defense that sits middle of the pack in WR fantasy points allowed.

Over/under: 58.2 (Highest)

Win probability: Lions 60% (9th highest)

Los Angeles Rams @ Las Vegas Raiders
Projected score: Rams 29, Raiders 26

Lineup locks: Matthew Stafford, Kyren Williams, Ashton Jeanty, Puka Nacua, Brock Bowers

Fantasy Scoop: Davante Adams (hamstring) is expected to miss 6-10 weeks of action, which will free up roughly 20% of the Rams' targets and, perhaps more notably, a large chunk of the team's opportunities near the goal line as Adams has scored four touchdowns and is responsible for five of the team's nine end zone targets this season. Adams' absence figures to lead to even more reliance on Nacua, but it's possible the rest of usage is spread around to the team's depth receivers and tight ends.

Konata Mumpfield is the next man up at receiver, but he managed only one good game while filling in for Adams during Weeks 16-18 last season (a 14-5-50-0 receiving line) and for Nacua during Weeks 2-3 this season (1-12-0 in Week 2, but 4-93-1 in Week 3). At best, Mumpfield is a speculative bench stash this weekend. TE duo Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee are now better bets to find the end zone, but the two share so much work that they don't make for viable fantasy starters either. Instead, keep Terrance Ferguson stashed on IR, as he could find his way into the TE1 mix if he's able to return in the near future.

Over/under: 55.3 (2nd highest)

Win probability: Rams 59% (10th highest)

Kansas City Chiefs @ Seattle Seahawks
Projected score: Chiefs 25, Seahawks 22

Lineup locks: Kenneth Walker III, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Xavier Worthy

Fantasy Scoop: After opening the season with 21.7 and 29.0 fantasy point efforts, Patrick Mahomes has faded to 15.9, 17.0 and 10.5 during his last three outings. Mahomes continues to play well, but the game script hasn't allowed much passing (no more than 30 passing attempts in four out of five games) and he hasn't added much with his legs (after posting a 7-23-1 rushing line in Week 1, he's totaled a 10-34-0 line over his last four games).

With Walker playing at an elite level, Kansas City has run a balanced offense (Andy Reid generally leans very pass-heavy) and has run the ball often near the goal line (56% of Chiefs touchdowns have been passes this year, compared to 69% during the prior Mahomes era). This week, Mahomes will face off with a Seattle defense that has allowed the fewest passing yards, lowest YPA (5.3) and second-fewest QB fantasy points this season. Seattle has held four of their opposing six QBs below 10.0 fantasy points.

Mahomes is a fringe fantasy starter most weeks but should absolutely be on benches against Seattle's elite defense.

Over/under: 47.2 (8th highest)

Win probability: Chiefs 58% (11th highest)

Dallas Cowboys @ Philadelphia Eagles
Projected score: Cowboys 26, Eagles 21

Lineup locks: Javonte Williams, Saquon Barkley, CeeDee Lamb, DeVonta Smith, George Pickens

Fantasy Scoop: Tanner McKee made his first start in place of Jalen Hurts (IR) last week and it certainly could have gone worse from a fantasy perspective. The 2023 sixth-round pick was inefficient (4.8 YPA, 58.0 C%) but attempted 45 passes, which allowed a strong fantasy showing from Smith (7-75-1 on 14 targets) and a solid outing from Dallas Goedert (6-61-0 on eight targets).

McKee was competent enough that we can feel secure with keeping Smith as a lineup lock against a Dallas defense that has allowed the third-highest EPA against the pass, as well as the seventh-most fantasy points to receivers. Goedert, meanwhile, has managed 12 catches on 17 targets over the two games since his return from injury and remains a back-end TE1.

Over/under: 47.2 (7th highest)

Win probability: Cowboys 65% (6th highest)

stories.headline: Nottingham Forest rue 'wrong' red card call, missed chances in Ipswich draw
stories.summary: Nottingham Forest lamented the referee's decision not to reduce Ipswich Town to 10 men in the second half, as well a number of missed chances in front of goal, after a 1-1 draw at Portman Road.
stories.body:
Nottingham Forest were left ruing the referee's decision not to reduce Ipswich Town to 10 men in the second half, as well a number of missed chances in front of goal, after a 1-1 draw at Portman Road on Friday.

The result lifted Forest out of the relegation zone but extended their winless run to four matches.

The big talking point was the 48th minute decision not to send off Issa Diop after he felled James McAtee as he headed towards the Ipswich goal. The video referee looked at the decision and Diop was yellow-carded.

"It was the wrong decision but we couldn't have played a more dominant second half," Forest coach Oliver Glasner told Sky Sports. "We created enough chances to decide the game and that's why I will never blame the referee.

"I liked that he went to the screen, this is the right procedure. It was wrong [decision] but he didn't do it on purpose."

On a blustery night, Forest played with the wind behind them during the first half and it was a swirling ball that led to the opener.

Daniel Muñoz threw in a high cross from the right and Neco Williams was unmarked in the box and guided his volley into the net.

Ipswich drew level four minutes before halftime when Nikola Milenkovic was caught in possession by Julio Enciso. The Paraguayan midfielder ran on to calmly slot the ball past diving goalkeeper Matz Sels.

Forest had the bulk of the chances in a gritty second period but could not make its superiority count.

"We have had so many good performances recently and we haven't been able to get the final three points and get over the line," Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White said. "Again tonight we had a lot of chances.

"The first half we were in control, then they were in control. But the second half we dominated completely and should have won the game, in my eyes. If we keep up these performances like this then the wins are going to have to come."

Forest have only one win in eight Premier League fixtures, which was also the case in the 2025-26 campaign and it led to owner Evangelos Marinakis dismissing Nuno Espirito Santo and Ange Postecoglou by this point last year.

However, Glasner struck a relaxed tone about the direction his team were heading in.

"Yes, the result, I think, doesn't reflect the performance, but I don't know a different solution than just to keep going because everyone sees, everyone feels we are on the right track, with the way we play, the way we create chances and also the way we defend," he told a news conference.

"[Now] it's supporting the players, keep the confidence and just waiting for this click. Maybe it's an own goal or a deflected ball like we lost last week because then the results will follow the performances."

Ipswich moved up one place to ninth in the table and manager Gary O'Neil acknowledged they had to dig deep to frustrate Forest.

"One where we had to show another side to get something from the game," O'Neil said. "One where togetherness, shutting up a little bit and being a bit safer got us through to the finish line. And proud of the players, because not easy to do that and a good point for us."

The Associated Press and PA contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 43
Goals: 40
Assists: 18

Oct. 17: Atlanta United 1-3 Inter Miami
Messi scored twice in four minutes as Miami won 3-1 in Atlanta.

After Germán Berterame opened the scoring just before halftime, Messi doubled Miami's lead in the 56th minute, exchanging passes with Berterame before weaving past a defender and firing a low left-footed shot into the net.

Messi struck again in the 60th minute, latching on to a pass from Luis Suárez before beating his marker and slotting past goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos. The brace took Messi's MLS-leading tally to 25 goals for the season, while Miami extended its winning streak to three matches.

Oct. 14: Inter Miami 2-0 NYCFC
No goals, but after a scoreless first half, Messi helped break the deadlock by setting up Rodrigo De Paul for the opening goal. Germán Berterame later doubled Miami's advantage as the Herons secured their second consecutive win and clinched a spot in the MLS playoffs.

Oct. 10: Inter Miami 4-0 D.C. United

Back in the pink of Inter Miami, and back in the goals for Messi.

His two strikes sealed an emphatic 4-0 win for the Herons over D.C. United at Nu Stadium on Saturday night.

After Luis Suárez had Miami 2-0 up after 39 minutes Messi scored his first in the 47th, retrieving a pass from the Uruguayan before tapping in a shot inside the right post.

Messi then padded the hosts' lead in the 60th minute, latching on to Rodrigo De Paul's pass, before dribbling inside the area, eluding two United defenders and firing past goalkeeper Sean Johnson with a shot from 12 yards.

Oct. 6: Argentina 3-0 Benin

It was an emotionally charged night in Buenos Aires as Messi played his final international match for Argentina, the team that he had led to World Cup glory and two Copa América titles as captain.

The friendly match at the Estadio Monumental was goalless at halftime, but just a few minutes after the break Messi's in-swinging corner from the left was rattled home on the volley by Nicolás Otamendi.

Then, on the hour mark, Messi spotted Nico Paz in space 25 yards from goal. He fed a square pass with the outside of his boot to the Como player, who curled in a classy finish.

But the night undoubtedly belonged to Messi, and he fired a penalty into the top corner to cap off his 208th and final senior appearance for his country with his 126th goal.

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami
Before heading to Argentina for his final international match, Messi gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: After two opposite fights, what should be expected from Yan vs. Dvalishvili 3
stories.summary: Merab Dvalishvili has tweaked his fight plan, while Yan has gone all-in on his. Which strategy will win out?
stories.body:
LAS VEGAS -- The UFC Performance Institute is nearly empty as Merab Dvalishvili wraps up his final round of sparring on a Saturday afternoon. He has been going for hours, switching among three partners after each five-minute round. Except for Dvalishvili's team, the place is deserted -- not because it's a slow day, but because it's technically closed. UFC staff was meant to clean and lock the doors 30 minutes ago, but Dvalishvili's workout is running long (as they tend to do). At this moment, though, the session appears finished. Coaches have turned their backs to the cage, and teammates are packing up their bags.

Then suddenly, a bell sounds and Dvalishvili walks out for another round of work. His seventh.

"I don't even know," head coach John Wood says when asked the maximum number of rounds he's ever witnessed Dvalishvili spar at once. "Just the other day he did 10, and I swear he could have done five more. We're not talking fluff rounds, either. We're talking 10 rounds, hard as f---.

"I really don't know who does that."

It could be that no one else does that. It's fair to wonder whether sparring 10 rounds at a time -- impressive as it might be -- is even a good idea. Such is the predicament of Merab "The Machine" Dvalishvili.

Dvalishvili pushed the limits of MMA history in 2025. He successfully defended the UFC's bantamweight championship three times in a span of 10 months, then attempted an unprecedented fourth title defense in a single calendar year in December. Dvalishvili ultimately fell short, losing his belt to Petr Yan in a five-round decision at UFC 323. Dvalishvili (21-5) will seek to recapture the belt when he faces Yan (20-5) for a third time Saturday at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (main card begins at 2 p.m. ET).

No UFC fighter has ever defended a title four times in a year, and none had even tried before Dvalishvili -- for good reason. To even attempt it, Dvalishvili had to walk a fine line between ambitious and foolish. He cut weight twice in 63 days for the December fight and concealed a significant knee injury from members of his team after UFC physicians told him he should consider withdrawing from the bout.

"Everything went bad," Dvalishvili admitted to ESPN. "I had the worst game plan, worst camp, worst training of any championship fight. But it's no excuse. I have no excuses. Yan beat me. I thought I could win and I took the fight, no regrets."

Dvalishvili's seemingly limitless capacity for work, pain and adversity has defined his career and endeared him to UFC fans. But that relentless drive can at times make the incredibly difficult sport of MMA even more challenging.

Dvalishvili's longtime training partner, former UFC bantamweight champion Aljamain Sterling, told ESPN he admires Dvalishvili's pursuit of history last year -- but he never thought it was a sound idea.

"I knew we were in trouble coming out of the gate," Sterling said. "I didn't have a good feeling about it. I honestly wasn't even as involved in that fourth camp, because I didn't think we were taking the fight. I had scheduled a few other commitments because I thought we were done for the year.

"You try to be as positive as you can be, but you're also like, 'I don't want to see my friend get hurt because we jumped into something we shouldn't have jumped into.'" Of course, it's impossible to determine beforehand how much is too much for someone such as Dvalishvili.

Wood, who has been in Dvalishvili's corner for more than five years, was certain it was too much in January 2025, when Dvalishvili was set to fight then-18-0 fighter Umar Nurmagomedov at UFC 311. A deep cut on Dvalishvili's leg developed staph infection during training camp, leading to what Wood described as one of the most unhealthy fight preparations he has ever been involved in. But Dvalishvili still went out and defeated Nurmagomedov in a five-round performance that earned him a fight of the night bonus. Dvalishvili rallied in the championship rounds to claim a decision.

"That's the fight I actually considered pulling him out of," Wood said. "He was so damaged in multiple ways for that one, and then went out there and performed like he did. Once he did that, he convinced me to really never question him again. In my mind, I was like, 'Oh s---, this guy really can do anything. He really is just a machine.'"

Dvalishvili's loss to Yan hasn't prompted a complete overhaul of the approach. He's still sparring 10 rounds in a single session, but it has refocused the camp in some ways.

Dvalishvili has said he needed a better game plan going into that fight. Perhaps, he said, the team overlooked Yan while in the midst of a 14-fight win streak that spanned eight years and included a physically dominant unanimous decision victory over Yan in their first career meeting. Dvalishvili logged a UFC record 49 takedown attempts in that March 2023 win.

The circumstances surrounding Dvalishvili and Yan's two fights combine for a complicated backdrop to the third meeting. They have spent 10 rounds together in the Octagon, but few conclusions can be drawn because of the opposite outcomes. After the first fight, both bantamweights said they competed through injuries, but Dvalishvili was the clear winner. Yan decisively won the second bout -- claiming four of five rounds on two judges' scorecards -- but Dvalishvili was presumably compromised. Ahead of the trilogy, Sterling said the team has worked on improving Dvalishvili's ground control, allowing him to use his notorious gas tank more efficiently.

"I don't feel like there was a lot of emphasis on that in his last few camps," Sterling said. "I think we've done a better job at tightening up his wrestling base. If he can do half of the things I do when it comes to controlling guys once he gets them to the floor, it's going to be scary, because then you've got that infinite amount of cardio on top of it. That's a dangerous combination."

Yan, who spent the first half of this year recovering from back surgery, said tactics and mental preparation -- more than any physical improvements (or better health) -- will decide Saturday's contest.

On that front, Yan considers he and his team to have a distinct edge. After the last fight, his coach, Kairat Nurmagambetov, unveiled a digital strategy tree he built that outlined a detailed plan for nearly every potential scenario Dvalishvili might try in the Octagon. In a recent interview, Yan revealed that Nurmagambetov has expanded the playbook for the trilogy fight.

"This fight will be decided by fight IQ, mental strength and which fighter makes better decisions," Yan told ESPN, through a translator. "The second fight, I beat him. In the third, I will do the same."

It's a simple, interesting way to put it: Which fighter will make better decisions?

For Dvalishvili, that's always a loaded question. His questionable decision-making has been well-documented over the years -- at times hilariously so and often in ways that seem specific to him. Is sparring 10 rounds a good decision? Is hiding an injury from your own team? Is jumping into a frozen lake head first, as Dvalishvili famously did in 2021?

The answer for Dvalishvili might be relative when compared to other fighters. Dvalishvili's mindset about work and his willingness to fight injured are unlikely to change, but the loss to Yan did make him rethink certain strategies.

Over the course of Dvalishvili's title reign, he shocked much of the MMA world by choosing to spar five rounds at full speed on the morning of his championship fights. He did so in December, before losing to Yan. When asked if he expects to continue that tradition, Dvalishvili admitted that is one specific quirk that is likely retired for good.

"I'm not going to spar this time," Dvalishvili said. "Especially against Petr Yan, I need all of my energy. When I did the five rounds before our last fight, that was probably a mistake. But I learned and now I will fix it. I felt good doing it, but I think there is a smarter way."

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes' home burgled during Man United loss against Como
stories.summary: Bruno Fernandes returned from Italy after losing to Como with Manchester United in the early hours of Thursday morning and had to deal with a robbery at his house.
stories.body:
Police are investigating a burglary at Bruno Fernandes' home which took place as he returned from Italy with Manchester United after losing to Como.

Fernandes' family are understood not to have been in the house at the time and police quickly attended the scene, with United supporting their skipper.

A statement from Cheshire Police, given to ESPN, read: "At around 8.30 p.m. on Wednesday Oct. 21, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property.

"Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.

"An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing."

Detective Inspector David Jarvis of Macclesfield Proactive CID said: "This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we're committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

"As part of our enquiries were keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.

"The same goes for anyone with any CCTV or dashcam footage which may aid the investigation."

Bruno Fernandes questions Man United tactics

A catastrophic night in Lombardy saw United suffer a humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas' side, which extended their winless run to seven fixtures and led to Fernandes publicly questioning the approach of boss Michael Carrick.

The result, alongside Fernandes' comments, had raised serious questions about Carrick's future ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but he will remain in charge for that match, sources told ESPN.

United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season's performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick's tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week's remarks by Lisandro Martínez.

Fernandes claimed it was the staff's decision "not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind" in Como.
